## Other ideas under consideration

**Ideas under consideration.** Raised for assessment; each stays open until it is decided, then moves to the tab of its system. An entry decided in part keeps its open part here.

- **A trade system** (decided 21 October 2026: "Economy and resources" under Land, people and economy, with caravans that can be intercepted, merchants and tolls). Only the waters it reaches beyond the Mediterranean are still open, below: the Persian Gulf matters most and the Red Sea a little, and the far ends of these waters are edge markets ("Edge markets").
- **Seas beyond the Mediterranean** (noted 21 October 2026; trade decided 21 October 2026). Until item 7a all the sea zones are in the Mediterranean and no boats use the rivers; item 7a adds the Gulf's sea zone and river waters for boats ("Rivers").
  - **The Persian Gulf and Dilmun.** In this period Dilmun (Bahrain) was held by the Kassite kings of Babylonia, with a governor of their own whose letters were found at Nippur, so it needs no new kingdom. It is on the map from the start as Babylonia's land, with its Gulf sea zone ("The edges of the map" under "Map review"). Through Dilmun ran the route to Magan (Oman) and its copper, a rival source to Cyprus's that would lessen Alashiya's leverage over every court that needs copper. Magan itself stays off the map, as the far end of the route. With the economy, Magan is an edge market at the Gulf's far end: it sells a little copper, a small alternative to Alashiya's since the Magan trade had shrunk by this period, and buys grain and gold ("What each edge trades" under Economy and resources). Babylonia's harbours on the Gulf earn its tolls, and Elam's coast on the same waters makes a rivalry at sea between Babylonia and Elam possible under the same rules. The two fought for centuries: a generation before 1346 a Kassite Kurigalzu took Susa (Chronicle P names Kurigalzu II, but the conquest is now usually given to Kurigalzu I), and some two centuries after it, around 1158 BCE, Shutruk-Nahhunte of Elam sacked Babylon.
  - **The Red Sea.** Egypt's route to Punt, for incense and rare goods; it mattered more a century before the Amarna letters, under Hatshepsut, so it is a minor addition at most. With the economy, it is a later addition (built in build order item 11c, decided 29 October 2026): one sea zone, with Punt as a door for newcomers but no market, since its gold would be new gold and its incense and ebony are not resources ("What each edge trades" under Economy and resources). Egypt has it alone, so it would see no war at sea, by the same rule that makes the Mediterranean contested: war at sea needs at least two powers with ships on the same waters, and Arabia's coast held no state of the Amarna world.
  - **The Aegean's far shore.** Ahhiyawa, the Mycenaean Greeks beyond the western sea, mattered more to Arzawa and Hatti in the following century; today it is the edge of the map. With the economy, it is the western edge market, selling the western share of tin ("What each edge trades" under Economy and resources), which arrives on Arzawa's coast, at Alashiya and in the Levantine ports. Crete belongs to this edge, not to the map (decided 21 October 2026). Knossos was under Mycenaean Greek rule by 1346, with its records in Linear B; the Egyptians called the Cretans Keftiu, Theban tomb paintings show them bringing gifts, and a statue base of Amenhotep III lists Knossos, Amnisos, Phaistos, Kydonia, Mycenae and Kythera, a sign of an Egyptian embassy to the Aegean in these very decades. But no letter in the archive came from Keftiu or from Ahhiyawa, so Crete traded with the world of the letters without taking part in it, and the bar for a province ("What earns a place" under "Map review") leaves it off. The edge market carries the period's own name, "Keftiu and Ahhiyawa", and its tin reaches the map by the open-sea crossings to Alashiya, Ugarit and Egypt, the way the Aegean pottery and oil travelled east in great quantity (goods the game leaves out of trade: "What each edge trades"). A later scenario with Ahhiyawa as a player, as it became for the Hittites in the following century, would bring Crete onto the map as a province.
  - **Not the Black Sea:** the Hittite north coast was held by the hostile Kaska, with little seafaring.

  Dilmun's dates and the governor's letters are from memory; the historical sources pass (build order item 6+) checks them.
- **A written strategy for model kings** (under consideration, 20 October 2026; **not to be built now**, nor as part of any build order item). Today all seven model kings are the same mind in different seats, with no temperament of their own. If, once the build order is done and Haakon has played, they feel too alike, each could be given a strategy for winning drawn from his position, as characters get theirs ("Stakes, not dispositions"): "a kingdom ringed by rivals wins by alliances and patience", never "you are cautious". The simulations show kings need no further priming to play hard; where they erred, they lacked information, not nerve.
